learning_question: In a survivorship-free point-in-time US universe, does the frozen value screen's buy tier (buy + strong_buy) beat a plain top-30% earnings-yield sort of the same names, after costs on both? Both legs carry the same value exposure, so the answer does not hinge on whether value or growth led the period. Whether value beats the market is the published factor question (value-factor-base-rate.md); the spread over the equal-weight universe is reported as context, split by value regime.
universe: S&P 500 members on each rebalance date (Sharadar sp500 table), common stock, active and delisted. Financials and real estate included, as in the live screen; reported split by sector.

data_source.vendor: Sharadar personal-use licence (sharadar.com), Core US Equities Bundle, full history
data_source.fundamentals: fundamentals table, dimension ART (as-reported trailing twelve months), latest row with filing date (datekey, or date in newer exports) at least 2 days before the rebalance date. Rows filed more than 456 days before the rebalance, and non-USD reporters, are dropped and counted.
data_source.prices: stocks table closeadj (split, dividend and spinoff adjusted) for total return. Market cap is the filing-date marketcap rolled to the rebalance by the split-adjusted close ratio, so splits between filing and rebalance cancel.
data_source.metric_mapping: Yahoo conventions as the live library screen receives them: dividend_yield and debt_to_equity in percent (2.5 = 2.5%), margins, returns and growth as fractions. revenue_growth and earnings_growth are quarterly year-on-year from ARQ (Yahoo's definition), falling back to ART year-on-year. *_prev fields come from the ART row one year earlier. Implemented in src/value_investor/sharadar_replay_adapter.py.
data_source.delistings: tickers isdelisted = Y. Merger exits for the sensitivity variant: actions acquisitionby or mergerto (ticker) and mergerfrom or acquisitionof (contraticker).
data_source.licence_handling: Raw tables stay outside the repository and are deleted within 30 days of cancelling. Only cohort-level aggregates are committed.

rebalance.cadence: last trading day of each month

holdout.reveal_rule: Revealed once, after the development window is reviewed and nothing in this file has changed. Later reveals are exploratory.

primary.secondary_role: context: the buy tier over the equal-weight universe, net of costs. Reported with the value_regime split; it does not decide the verdict.
primary.pass_bar: Holdout 90% interval on the primary metric lies wholly above zero, and the 365-day holdout primary is not wholly below zero (the monthly edge over the plain sort does not reverse over a year).

comparators.plain_value: equal-weight top 30% by positive earnings yield (earnings_yield_pe) among the same names, charged the same cost per side on its own turnover. The decision comparator.
comparators.universe: equal-weight return of every name with entry and exit prices; costless. Context only.
comparators.value_regime: each cohort is labelled value_led when the plain sort beat the universe gross, value_lagged otherwise; the primary and the market spread are summarised in each. Descriptive, not a pass bar.

costs.model: Each leg pays 2 x cost x its own turnover versus its set one horizon earlier: buy_minus_plain_value_net = (buy-tier spread - 2c x buy-tier turnover) - (plain spread - 2c x plain turnover). The universe comparator is costless.
costs.source: Base is the fair S&P 500 cost for this GBP-funded investor from market_trading_costs (sp500, t212_invest_fair_v1): about 0.15% FX per conversion plus a 0.025% half-spread, 0.175% per side. Stress is 3% per side.

delisting.rule: A name whose prices end before the exit date exits at its last adjusted close times (1 + haircut). Baseline 0; sensitivity -30% for delistings that were not mergers or acquisitions.

fixed_rules: No threshold, weight, or model search on any window (N33).
Model weights stay at defaults; the 28-day learner is not run (N197).
Per-model rank IC may be reported but never tunes the screen.
Any change to this file or to the fingerprinted screen code after the holdout is revealed opens a new registration_id; its results are exploratory.

decisions.beats_plain_value: The screen's machinery (sector-relative ranks, pass count, quality and risk vetoes) adds to textbook value after costs: keep it; multi-year total return becomes the fitness test N197 asks for.
decisions.inconclusive: No measurable gain over the plain sort: freeze the screen's machinery (no new extras) and let forward evidence and the AI layer earn their keep separately.
decisions.loses_to_plain_value: The extras cost money over textbook value: simplify toward the published sort before stage 4.
decisions.market_context: The spread over the universe and its value_regime split are read beside the verdict, never instead of it. A negative market spread in a value_lagged decade with a positive primary is a value-regime result, not a screen failure.

amendments.change: data_source spelled out to match the Phase 2 adapter: market cap rolled by split-adjusted close (replaces close x sharesbas, which breaks across splits), Yahoo unit conventions including percent dividend yield, quarterly growth, staleness and currency exclusions, merger classification.
Base cost 0.53% -> 0.175% per side (stress 3% unchanged). library_screen.py added to the fingerprinted screen code.
amendments.reason: 0.53% is the FTSE 350 round trip (0.5% stamp duty), not a US per-side cost; it overstated US costs about threefold. library_screen.py runs the replayed pipeline (load, derived columns, scoring order, stability), so a change there must stale the registration and the signal cache. No licensed data has been used.

amendments.change: Primary metric buy_tier_spread_net -> buy_minus_plain_value_net (the plain sort now pays the same costs on its own turnover). The market spread becomes secondary context with a value_regime split. A 365-day confirmation verdict is computed. Decisions reworded around the plain sort.
amendments.reason: The holdout (2013-2025) is a decade in which value lagged growth. Scoring the screen against the market would mostly measure that regime, which the published value base rate already covers. Both legs of buy-minus-plain carry the same value exposure, so it isolates what this project controls. No licensed data has been used and no holdout has been revealed.
